claims.quote: large advertisers will combine in the future to own papers confined to the advertisements of their specific wares
claims.description: Large advertisers will come to own newspapers devoted solely to advertising their own products (reported as a supposition, which the author rejects).

claims.quote: this anticipation of the advertiser-owned paper, like that of hourly papers, and that wonderfully powerful cosmic newspaper syndicate, is simply another instance of prophesying based only on a present trend
claims.description: Hourly newspapers and a hugely powerful worldwide newspaper syndicate are named as predictions the author dismisses as unlikely.

claims.quote: One can conceive it provided in the future with cross-thread telescopic sights, the focussing of which, corrected by some ingenious use of hygroscopic material, might even find the range
claims.description: Rifles will have telescopic sights that automatically find range, allowing accurate fire at a mile or more.

claims.quote: It will be used either for single shots or to quiver and send a spray of almost simultaneous bullets out of a magazine evenly and certainly, over any small area the rifleman thinks advisable.
claims.description: Rifles will gain automatic or burst-fire capability like machine guns.

claims.quote: It will, just as probably, be slung with its ammunition and equipment upon bicycle wheels, and be the common care of two or more associated soldiers.
claims.description: Rifles will be crew-served weapons mounted on bicycle wheels.

claims.quote: this will be the opening phase of the struggle, a vast duel all along the frontier between groups of skilled marksmen, continually being relieved and refreshed from the rear.
claims.description: Future wars between neighbouring states will open with long frontier duels between small groups of dug-in marksmen rather than cavalry charges and pitched battles.
claims.stated_time: the war that is speedily to come

claims.quote: somewhere far in the rear the central organizer will sit at the telephonic centre of his vast front, and he will strengthen here and feed there
claims.description: Battles will be directed by a commander at a telephone hub far behind the front, with no general in the field.

claims.quote: all along those great motor roads our first "[…]" sketched, there will be a vast and rapid shifting to and fro of big and very long range guns.
claims.description: Very long-range heavy guns will be moved rapidly along great motor roads to reinforce threatened sectors.

claims.quote: The latter will hang above the firing line all along the front, incessantly ascending and withdrawn; they will be continually determining the distribution of the antagonist's forces, directing the fire of continually shifting great guns
claims.description: Observation balloons along the front will spot for long-range artillery and reveal enemy dispositions.

claims.quote: a practical realization of socialistic conceptions will quite inevitably be forced upon the fighting State.
claims.description: Total war will force states to take over industry, transport, food and clothing supply, drafting all able-bodied citizens and resources into war organization.

claims.quote: there will be a very considerable restriction of the rights of the non-combatant.
claims.description: Future war will erase the distinction between combatants and civilians, with the whole state mobilized and civilians' protections reduced.

claims.quote: The spontaneous traffic of the roads in peace, will fall now into two streams, one of women and children coming quietly and comfortably out of danger, the other of men and material going up to the front.
claims.description: At the outbreak of war, women and children will be evacuated from danger zones in an orderly, pre-planned manner while men and supplies move to the front.

claims.quote: As the bells ring and the recording telephones click into every house the news that war has come
claims.description: News of war will be delivered into every home by telephones that record messages.

claims.quote: Certainly they will be steerable. Moreover, when the wind admits, there will be freely-moving steerable balloons wagging little flags to their friends below.
claims.description: Military balloons will be dirigible and steerable.

claims.quote: Few people, I fancy, who know the work of Langley, Lilienthal, Pilcher, Maxim, and Chanute, but will be inclined to believe that long before the year a.d. 2000, and very probably before 1950, a successful aeroplane will have soared and come home safe and sound.
claims.description: A successful heavier-than-air aeroplane will fly and return safely by 1950 at the latest, probably earlier, and will be applied to war.
claims.stated_time: long before the year a.d. 2000, and very probably before 1950

claims.quote: Directly that is accomplished the new invention will be most assuredly applied to war.
claims.description: Aeroplanes will be used as weapons of war as soon as they are achieved.

claims.quote: I am inclined to think the practicable navigable balloon will be first attained by the use of a device already employed by Nature in the swimming-bladder of fishes.
claims.description: A dirigible aircraft using contractile gas bags modeled on fish swim bladders, combined with winged cars and engine-driven screws, will achieve controlled flight.

claims.quote: I incline to imagine there will be a steel prow with a cutting edge at either end of the sort of aerostat I foresee, and conceivably this aerial ram will be the most important weapon of the affair.
claims.description: Armed airships will fight in the sky, ramming enemy balloons and each other, with crews carrying parachutes.

claims.quote: It would probably have at most a small machine-gun or so, which might fire an explosive shell at the balloons of the enemy, or kill their aeronauts with distributed bullets.
claims.description: Combat airships will carry small machine guns firing explosive shells in aerial combat.

claims.quote: Once the command of the air is obtained by one of the contending armies, the war must become a conflict between a seeing host and one that is blind.
claims.description: Air superiority will decide wars by giving the victor total observation of the enemy and blinding the loser.

claims.quote: By day the victor's aeroplanes will sweep down upon the apparatus of all sorts in the adversary's rear, and will drop explosives and incendiary matters upon them
claims.description: Aircraft will bomb enemy rear areas with explosive and incendiary bombs, leaving no camp or shelter safe.

claims.quote: At night his high floating search-lights will go to and fro and discover and check every desperate attempt to relieve or feed the exhausted marksmen of the fighting line.
claims.description: Airborne searchlights will illuminate enemy supply movements at night.

claims.quote: ironclad road fighting-machines may perhaps play a considerable part in this
claims.description: Armoured fighting vehicles will operate on roads during the advance.

claims.quote: It will probably be brought about in a civilized country by the seizure of the vital apparatus of the urban regions—the water supply, the generating stations for electricity (which will supply all the heat and warmth of the land), and the chief ways used in food distribution.
claims.description: Victors will force surrender by seizing water supplies, electricity generating stations and food distribution; electricity will supply all heating.

claims.quote: I seem to see a light type of ironclad, armoured thickly only over its engines and magazines, murderously equipped, and with a ram—as alert and deadly as a striking snake.
claims.description: Future naval war will favor fast, lightly armoured ironclads with rams focused on speed, range and fire precision.

claims.quote: The struggle on the high seas between any two naval powers (except, perhaps, the English and American, who have both quite unparalleled opportunities for coaling) will not last more than a week or so.
claims.description: Future naval wars will be decided within about a week through destruction, blockade or cutting off of coal supply.

claims.quote: I think the possibilities of that sort of thing are greatly exaggerated.
claims.description: Commerce-destroying raiders will be quickly hunted down and sunk, so commerce raiding won't pay.

claims.quote: And then will open a second phase of naval warfare, in which the submarine may play a larger part.
claims.description: After surface command of the sea is settled, submarines will play a larger role in naval warfare.

claims.quote: Recruiting among the working classes—or, more properly speaking, among the People of the Abyss—will have dwindled to the vanishing point
claims.description: Modern war's complexity will make unskilled lower-class recruits useless and recruiting from them will end.
